subject: Copywriting
title: The Welcome Sequence
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Welcome Sequence.

hook.text: Welcome emails get 4x more opens and 5x more clicks than regular emails. The first email sets the entire relationship.

buildup.text: A welcome sequence runs 3 to 7 emails over the first two weeks.

discovery.text: Email 1: deliver the promise. Email 2: tell your story. Email 3: prove your value. Email 4: make the offer.

twist.text: Most brands send one welcome email and stop. The sequence is where relationships are built.

climax.text: Companies with welcome sequences see 33% more long-term engagement than those with a single welcome email.

punchline.text: 4x opens, 5x clicks. The welcome email is your best first impression.

quiz.question: How many more clicks do welcome emails get compared to regular emails?

details.summary: A welcome sequence is a series of automated emails sent to new subscribers in their first days. It is the highest-performing email type, with open rates 4x higher than regular campaigns. The sequence should introduce the brand, deliver promised value, set expectations, and move subscribers...
details.whyItMatters: New subscribers are most engaged in their first 48 hours. A strong welcome sequence capitalizes on this peak attention to build habit, trust, and conversion — missing this window wastes your best opportunity.
takeaways: Welcome emails achieve 4x higher open rates than regular campaigns
The first 48 hours after signup are the peak engagement window
A good sequence delivers value before making any sales ask

faq.question: How many emails should a welcome sequence include?
faq.answer: Three to five emails over the first one to two weeks is standard. Email 1 delivers the promised lead magnet. Email 2 introduces the brand story. Email 3 provides social proof. Emails 4-5 guide toward the first purchase or key action.

faq.question: Why do welcome emails outperform regular campaigns?
faq.answer: New subscribers have just taken an action — signing up — that signals high interest. They are expecting an email, so open rates spike. Their curiosity about the brand is at its peak. This combination of expectation, interest, and recency creates unmatched engagement.
